meta.note: Demo deck — Ryan Howard @ Sabre (The Office characters)

cards.question: Walk me through your background.
cards.referenceAnswer: Seven years in platform engineering — started at Dunder Mifflin IT, founded WUPHF where I learned scale the hard way, then Vance Refrigeration Cloud where I led printer sync migration cutting stale config from fourteen hours to four minutes across a hundred twenty thousand devices, and built an SDK nine teams adopted. I'm here for staff scope on Sabre's connected devices platform because I don't want another seventy-two-hour outage on my watch.
cards.myAnswer: I've done platform work at Vance and WUPHF, led a sync migration, built an SDK. I want staff scope at Sabre.
cards.aiCoaching:
**Strong bones.** Lead with **14h → 4min** and **120K devices** in sentence one. Name the **72-hour outage** as why Sabre now. Drop filler — Pam said tighten the opener.

**Model opener:** "Seven years building device platforms — most recently I cut config staleness from fourteen hours to four minutes on a hundred twenty thousand units and shipped an SDK nine field teams adopted. I'm back at Sabre for staff scope on the guild that prevents another multi-day outage."

cards.question: Why do you want to work for Jim Halpert specifically?
cards.referenceAnswer: Jim runs the team the way good platform teams should run — sustainable on-call, clarity over fire drills, and he actually uses the SDK we built for field teams. I want a manager who protects deep work while still shipping. His team owns the problem I care about: config drift at scale.

cards.question: Michael Scott asks what 'world's best printer cloud' means to you. What do you say?
cards.referenceAnswer: One metric: p99 config freshness under thirty seconds fleet-wide, with rollback that doesn't brick devices. Culture-wise: field teams adopt the platform because it's easier than scripts — nine teams on the SDK proved that. I'd ask Michael which part of that vision he wants staff to own first.
cards.myAnswer: I'd say reliable sync and happy developers.
cards.aiCoaching: **Too vague for Michael's final.** Give a **number** (p99 < 30s) and **proof** (9 teams, zero bricked rollout). Echo his phrase then land substance — he respects sincerity plus specifics.

cards.question: Dwight asks you to whiteboard the printer sync migration.
cards.referenceAnswer: Dual-write phase: devices report to old batch path and new stream; compare counts per region; feature-flag cutover by geography; rollback keeps last-known-good firmware pointer. Result: fourteen hours to four minutes, zero bricked devices. Idempotent workers because Dwight will ask twice.

cards.question: Tell me about a failure.
cards.referenceAnswer: WUPHF — we hit two million messages a month without queue backpressure or paging. We went down during a demo. I wrote the postmortem, added backpressure and dashboards, and I've started every platform design since with failure modes first. That's why Sabre's outage week resonates — I won't skip observability again.
